observable_outcome: The M5 local closure is provable without a deploy and without a promotion: a Release Candidate bundle has an immutable digest over declared members in seven roles (contract, schema, api-contract, implementation-manifest, migration, configuration, documentation), computed from source bytes so no caller can assert it; the promotion gate re-verifies the bundle against the source tree, so a candidate whose candidate-side and evidence-side documentation digests were both fabricated is refused where it previously promoted to stable; a one-byte change to any documentation member stops promotion and stops Requirement completion, while a one-byte change to a file in no role changes nothing; the candidate's capability set is derived from the compiled Release Contract, so the real Foundation baseline candidate is provably not promotable while all twelve capabilities carry empty evidence_ids, and evidence for eleven of twelve is refused by name; rollback restores the previous stable route, records why, and can no longer be undone by a second rollback, so returning forward requires a fresh gate pass; a completed Requirement's StableSnapshot is bound to a bundle held in the store and to a stable documentation route, and a refused gate's zero proof cannot complete anything; Preview and Stable documentation routing is machine-checked for link and anchor resolution, release-marker agreement with the contract, capability-anchor bijection in both directions, the four required Preview sections, absence of Stable-to-Preview references and code-block allowlisting; retention eligibility refuses a routed version, an open rollback window and a version a Requirement still references; and devbox run --pure -- make check is green at the committed checkpoint with .agents/v2/evidence/V2-021-release.json registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json.
acceptance_criteria: A1. All 3 top-level tests currently in internal/release (TestCompileFoundationBaselineContract, TestBundleImmutableRouteAndRollback, TestContractAndPromotionGateRejectDriftAndStaleEvidence) and all 14 in internal/contracts still exist under the same names and still pass. Do not rewrite, rename or re-prove any of them, and do not edit any existing test body: the new claims go in new test functions. State the before and after top-level test counts for internal/release in the evidence summary; the measured pre-change counts are 3 (internal/release) and 14 (internal/contracts) at HEAD 576019e.

A2. The measured defect is pinned by a regression test. Before the change, a candidate whose candidate.DocsDigest and every evidence[i].DocsDigest were both set to the fabricated string 'drifted-docs' was promoted by PromotionGate to status stable with a nil error, because PromotionGate(bundle, control, permit) never receives documentation bytes and domain.CanPromote only compares the candidate against its own evidence. A new test asserts that such a candidate is now refused because the bundle no longer verifies against the source tree, and the evidence summary states the before and after explicitly.

A3. internal/release/bundle.go defines the bundle manifest exactly as dp-v2-021 d3 specifies: a Member is (role, repository-relative path, sha256 of bytes); the seven roles are contract (contracts/release-contract/**), schema (contracts/schemas/**), api-contract (contracts/openapi/**), implementation-manifest (ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.lock), migration (firestore.indexes.json), configuration (devbox.json, firebase.json) and documentation (docs/preview/**.md, docs/stable/**.md); BundleDigest is sha256 over the framing role\x00path\x00hexdigest\n for all members sorted by (role, path) and DocsDigest is the same framing restricted to role documentation. Assert: two assemblies of the same tree produce byte-identical digests; a member list built in a shuffled order produces the same digest; a symlinked member is refused; a declared member that does not exist is refused; a role that resolves to zero members is refused; and a path escaping the root is refused. CompileContract's signature is unchanged and the assembly passes the documentation framing bytes as its docs argument, so CompiledContract.DocsDigest equals the doc-set digest by construction.

A4. The guarded/unguarded partition is machine-checked and self-declaring. A test in internal/release parses ci/components.json directly (no import of internal/ci) and recomputes the release component's evidence-key closure exactly as internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() does: the component's roots, public_contracts and contract_dependencies, the public_contracts of each declared dependency, plus the unconditional ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock. Assert that the measured closure covers internal/release/**, contracts/** and those four files; that every bundle member is either inside the closure or listed in an explicit UnguardedMembers allowlist naming docs/preview/**.md, docs/stable/**.md, firestore.indexes.json, devbox.json and firebase.json with the reason; that a member which is neither fails the test; and that an allowlisted member which becomes guarded also fails the test, so escalation E1's fix must delete the entry. Do not delete an allowlist entry to make a test pass.

A5. The docs drift gate is proven hermetically with a negative control. In a synthetic repository tree under t.TempDir(): assemble a candidate with full capability evidence, promote it through Pipeline.Promote and assert it reaches stable; then flip one byte in one documentation member and assert (a) DocsDigest changed, (b) VerifySource refuses and its error names the drifted member path, (c) the candidate assembled before the edit no longer passes CanPromote because its capability evidence is no longer fresh, (d) Pipeline.Promote returns an error and Router generation is unchanged, and (e) as the mandatory negative control, flipping a byte in a file matching no role glob leaves BundleDigest and DocsDigest unchanged. Without (e) the test would also pass for a whole-tree hash, which would make every unrelated commit a docs drift; state that reasoning in the work report.

A6. Evidence freshness follows validation.md section 8 per role. One subtest per role asserts that changing any member's bytes invalidates every capability evidence bound to the previous candidate digest, and one negative control asserts that changing a file in no role invalidates nothing. The invalidation must be computed from the digests, not from a boolean the test sets.

A7. The candidate's capability set is derived, not supplied. AssembleCandidate takes ReleaseCandidate.Capabilities from CompiledContract.Capabilities in contract order and VerifyCandidateAgainstContract refuses any candidate whose set differs. Assert three cases: the real-tree Foundation candidate declares exactly the twelve baseline ids in contract order; a candidate with evidence for eleven of twelve is refused with the missing capability id named; and a hand-built candidate declaring the single capability 'healthz' bound to the real contract and docs digests is refused. The measured pre-change behaviour of that third case is that it promoted to status stable with a nil error while the contract declared twelve capabilities; record the before and after.

A8. Rollback is monotonic. Measured pre-change behaviour: after SetPreview/Promote of v1 then v2, the first Rollback produced {PreviewDigest:v2 StableDigest:v1 PreviousStableDigest:v2 Generation:5} and a second Rollback returned StableDigest to v2 with a nil error at Generation 6, re-promoting a withdrawn digest with no gate pass. After the change, Rollback restores the previous stable, clears the forward pointer, and records a RollbackRecord (repository, from digest, to digest, reason, at); a second consecutive Rollback is refused; and moving forward again requires SetPreview plus a full Promote through the gate. TestBundleImmutableRouteAndRollback must keep passing without any edit, because it rolls back exactly once; if it needs editing, the change is wrong.

A9. The previous stable documentation set stays resolvable after a rollback. Assert that after a rollback the restored version's doc set resolves as the stable channel, the withdrawn version's doc set is still retained while its rollback window is open, and the default channel resolution is stable when a stable release exists and preview otherwise.

A10. Retention eligibility has three independent refusals and one positive case, over an injected clock and a contract-declared rollback window, never the clock alone: refuse while the version is the current stable route target; refuse while it is the previous stable route target; refuse while its rollback window is open; refuse while any Requirement's StableSnapshot references it; and accept only when none of those hold. Each refusal has its own assertion so a single boolean cannot hide two of them.

A11. Requirement completion is chained to the gate. Assert: a refused gate returns the zero StableReleaseProof and CompleteRequirementFromRelease then refuses with ErrEvidenceIncomplete, so a docs-drifted candidate can never complete a Requirement; a completed Requirement's StableSnapshot BundleDigest and EvidenceDigest equal the bundle stored under that candidate id in the Store; after completion the router's stable digest equals the completed snapshot's candidate digest and the default documentation channel resolves to stable; and when the completion step fails the router generation is unchanged, so no half-promoted state exists. Do not re-prove that completion is reachable only from evaluating with a valid proof: V2-010's BFS already owns that claim and the work report must cite it rather than repeat it.

A12. Preview and Stable documentation routing is machine-verified with deterministic checks only. Assert over the real doc set: every relative markdown link resolves to an existing file (measured: 5 links today, 3 to contracts/release-contract/foundation.json and 2 to capabilities.md); every path#anchor link resolves to exactly one ; the capability anchor set of docs/preview/capabilities.md is bijective with the contract's twelve capability ids in both directions, where the document-to-contract direction is the new claim; each channel index declares a fixed-format release marker, the preview marker equals the contract's release string 0.1.0-baseline and the stable marker is 'none' exactly while no capability has status stable; docs/preview/stable-diff.md contains the four required sections (difference from Stable, known issues, how to return to Stable, evidence still missing for promotion); no document under docs/stable/** links into docs/preview/**; and fenced code blocks are extracted and checked against a command allowlist. The real doc set contains zero fenced blocks today, so the extractor must additionally be exercised on a synthetic fixture that does contain blocks, and the real-tree assertion is the falsifiable 'zero blocks now, any future block must be allowlisted'. No AI document review is used or reported as a check.

A13. Documentation edits are confined to docs/preview/index.md, docs/preview/stable-diff.md and docs/stable/index.md. docs/preview/capabilities.md is prohibited so the twelve anchors TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline resolves exactly once cannot move; docs/preview/README.md is prohibited. The release marker is a fixed, documented line format parsed by the test, not free prose. No digest value appears anywhere in the doc set, because a documentation member containing its own digest is an unsatisfiable fixpoint. make docs and make component-docs stay green.

A14. Two journeys, each one self-contained top-level test function in internal/release/journey_test.go with its own t.TempDir() fixtures, its own context deadline, an injected clock and no package-level mutable state. Journey 1, release segment: assemble from a synthetic tree, set the preview route, record capability evidence for every declared capability, pass the gate, promote the route, complete the Requirement from the proof, and assert the stable documentation channel is the default. Journey 7, local segment: a Preview regression withdraws the candidate, rollback restores the previous stable route and its doc set, and a Requirement is resumed against the restored stable snapshot. No fixed sleep, no timer, no goroutine, no dependence on another test's order. The work report must state that journey 7's live half, intentionally breaking a deployed Preview, is V2-022 and is untouched here.

A15. A real-tree conformance test assembles the Foundation candidate from the repository root and asserts the honest negative result: all seven roles resolve to at least one member, the documentation role resolves to exactly the files matching its globs (measured: docs/preview/README.md, docs/preview/capabilities.md, docs/preview/index.md, docs/preview/stable-diff.md, docs/stable/index.md), the contract compiles with release 0.1.0-baseline and the twelve baseline capability ids, and the assembled candidate is NOT promotable because every capability has status preview with empty evidence_ids, with the refusal naming missing capability evidence. Report the member count rather than pinning it. Do not fabricate capability evidence for the real tree to make this pass.

A16. Boundaries hold. internal/domain non-test files, contracts/**, ci/**, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.json, devbox.lock, internal/application/**, internal/store/**, internal/api/**, internal/update/** and internal/ci/** are unchanged; no new component is added; test/journeys/ is not created. internal/release/source_guard_test.go asserts with go/ast, not text matching, that the package's non-test files import only the standard library plus internal/domain and that no file in the package imports internal/ci or internal/update; the matcher is verified against a known-positive and a known-negative import path and the test fails outright on a zero-file scan so it cannot pass vacuously. Record the file count scanned.

A17. docs/operations/release-local.md is updated to match the implementation and is the only document outside docs/preview and docs/stable that changes. It must state: the seven bundle roles and the digest framing; that the implementation identity at M5-local is the source manifest and not a built binary digest, which is V2-022 and V2-034; the guarded/unguarded member partition, the UnguardedMembers allowlist and escalation E1, plainly saying that a docs-only commit does not select the release component in selective CI and that the drift gate is therefore enforced by make check and not by a docs-only CI run; that rollback is monotonic and route-level, that domain.ReleaseAssembling, ReleasePreviewDeployed, ReleaseRejected and ReleaseRollback are constants no transition function produces (a recorded divergence, not a decision this task made, escalation E3), and that route rollback is deliberately not coupled to internal/update.Switch's channel symlink rollback, which is documented rather than imported; retention eligibility and its three refusals; and the fixpoint prohibition on digests in the doc set.

A18. Exactly one evidence record, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-021-release.json, with id ev-v2-021-release, task_id V2-021 (the producer), component release and result passed, one check per acceptance item above carrying the argv actually executed and its timeout, and artifact_refs holding the bundle digest, contract digest and doc-set digest of the real-tree Foundation candidate. Its evidence_key is the release component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree at which devbox run --pure -- make check, format included, is green, because a formatting-only change moves the key; one check summary additionally reports the docs component key from the same run. Register exactly one entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the record file's bytes, and confirm devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green. That pair, registered in the index and the ledger test green, is the definition of done, not merely that the tests passed.

A19. After committing the evidence, devbox run --pure -- make check is green on the committed state, because gitleaks git scans committed history and never scans an uncommitted working tree. Then devbox run --pure -- make candidate-affected is run and the observation recorded: the docs component's evidence key moved because this task edited three documents, so the candidate required fresh docs evidence. Checkpoints are pushed one at a time by the coordinator and the parent commit's v2 selective CI is confirmed green before the next push, per docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10.

A20. No acceptance item is reported as passed unless its argv was actually executed in this task, and no claim here substitutes for V2-022. The work report must state explicitly that V2-021 did not make this repository a Preview target, did not deploy any Preview, did not exercise any capability in a Preview environment, did not break a Preview or resume a Requirement on a real previous Stable, used no real Provider CLI, no GCP project and no credential, and that no Stable release exists; a synthetic tree and a non-promotable real-tree candidate are not evidence about a live release. The M5 completion conditions 'このFoundation RepositoryをPreview対象にしてdogfoodする' and 'Previewを意図的に壊し、旧StableでRequirementを再開する' remain owned by V2-022 and are untouched by this task.
constraints: Local closure only. Do not deploy, do not promote anything outside a test process, do not invoke codex, claude or opencode, do not touch a GCP project, and do not read any credential from the environment, a keyring or disk outside t.TempDir(). The task's non_goals are binding: no real deploy, no real promotion, and no substitution of schema and link verification by AI document review.

Determinism is an acceptance property, not a preference. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, no goroutine, and no dependence on another test's execution order. Use t.TempDir(), an injected clock and a per-test context deadline with t.Fatal on timeout. If a test cannot be made deterministic, stop and escalate; validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied, so do not quarantine and do not retry it into a pass.

Do not create test/journeys/ and do not edit ci/components.json. internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() hashes ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock into every component key, ci/** is in all_on_change, and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-040-candidate-aggregate.json pins all 23 component keys in its check summaries; ValidateTracked also requires exactly one owning component per tracked file, so test/journeys/** cannot exist without that edit and make ownership, part of make check, would fail.

internal/domain non-test files, contracts/schemas/**, contracts/release-contract/** and contracts/openapi/** are prohibited. The M1 gate proved closure over the domain files and V2-009 owns the contract baseline; reopening either is a cross-boundary redesign. If the assembly appears to need a new domain type, a new release status transition, a new PermitKind or a contract field, stop and escalate with the exact type and the reason.

internal/application, internal/store, internal/api and internal/reconciler are prohibited. There is no canonical release surface anywhere outside internal/domain and internal/release; creating one here is escalation E2, not implementation, and V2-019 holds the reconciler and application boundary open.

Do not import internal/update or internal/ci from internal/release, in test files or otherwise. The release component declares dependencies on domain and contracts only, so such an import would be a component edge the manifest does not record: a change there would neither select the release component nor move its evidence key. Document the relationship in release-local.md instead.
Do not write any task-state file. Sol owns every .agents/v2/task-state transition and the coordinator edits that directory concurrently. Report the exact block_reason string instead.

.agents/v2/evidence/index.json is being edited concurrently. Add only the single ev-v2-021-release entry, never rewrite or reorder another task's entry, and after any rebase recompute evidence_hash on the final bytes of the record file before declaring the ledger test green.

docs/architecture/**, docs/operations/runner-local.md, docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md, docs/preview/capabilities.md, docs/preview/README.md and every other evidence record are held open by other agents or by other tasks. Do not touch them.

Escalate to tech_lead, do not guess: any acceptance item whose target boundary, observable or validation entry point is unclear, and any second consecutive failure of the same acceptance item. The retry budget for this task is 2 attempts.

The five open escalations are named and must not be decided alone. E1: couple docs/preview/** and docs/stable/** to the release component so a docs-only commit selects it, which needs a ci/components.json edit and therefore a milestone boundary where 23-key re-evidencing is already being paid. E2: the canonical release aggregate, UnitOfWork and event/outbox projection in internal/application and internal/store that a live promotion needs. E3: domain.ReleaseAssembling, ReleasePreviewDeployed, ReleaseRejected and ReleaseRollback are constants no transition function produces, and there is no domain rollback transition. E4: the migration, configuration and future binary roles of the bundle cannot be source-guarded at M5-local. E5: any need to touch contracts/** or internal/domain non-test files. Raise a new question of the same kind rather than deciding it.

Rollback of this task is a single git revert of its checkpoint commits. No external state, no cloud resource, no credential and no deployed artifact is created, so nothing outside the repository needs undoing; the only side effects are files under the allowed paths.
Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree. Do not commit or push outside it; the coordinator pushes checkpoints one at a time and waits for the parent commit's CI.
Japanese for the tracked documents; English identifiers in code, schemas and configuration.
